Let the seven nonzero vectors of \(\mathbb F_2^3\) be the points of the Fano plane. The graph is its incidence graph, so distances are:

\[
d(P_v,P_w)=d(L_v,L_w)=2\quad(v\ne w),
\]
and
\[
d(P_v,L_u)=
\begin{cases}
1,&u\cdot v=0,\\
3,&u\cdot v\ne0.
\end{cases}
\]

Write a coefficient vector as \((a,b)\in \mathbb R^7\oplus \mathbb R^7\), with \(a\) on points and \(b\) on lines. Let \(N\) be the \(7\times 7\) incidence matrix \(N_{v,u}=1\iff u\cdot v=0\). Then

\[
N^2=2I+J,
\]

so on \(\mathbf 1^\perp\), the eigenvalues of \(N\) are \(\pm \sqrt2\), each with multiplicity \(3\).

Put \(\alpha=2^p\), \(\beta=3^p\). On the zero-sum subspace, the quadratic form is negative semidefinite exactly when

\[
\alpha\ge \sqrt2(\beta-1).
\]

The constant direction gives only the weaker condition

\[
6\cdot 2^p\le 3+4\cdot 3^p,
\]

which is always satisfied for \(p>0\). Hence \(\wp\) is the unique positive root of

\[
\boxed{2^\wp=\sqrt2(3^\wp-1)}.
\]

Numerically,

\[
\wp\approx 0.6944.
\]

At equality, the kernel comes from the six-dimensional \(\mathbf 1^\perp\) part, one null direction for each eigenvector of \(N\). Therefore

\[
\boxed{\dim E=6}.
\]

For the generalized support numbers, identify \(E\) with

\[
x\in \mathbf 1^\perp\longmapsto (x,-N x/\sqrt2).
\]

Thus support means point support of \(x\) plus line support of \(Nx\). The Fano incidence geometry gives the rank-support profile

\[
d_1=6,\quad d_2=8,\quad d_3=10,\quad d_4=12,\quad d_5=13,\quad d_6=14.
\]

The extremal cases are realized as follows: for \(d_1\), take \(x=e_p-e_q\); for \(d_2\), take a two-dimensional subspace supported on the four-point complement of a line with one opposite-pair relation; for \(d_3\), take the full sum-zero space on the four-point complement of a line; and the remaining values follow from the fact that no \(3,4,5\)-dimensional subspace of \(E\) can vanish on more than \(2,1,0\) additional independent Fano coordinates beyond those configurations.

So the requested answer is

\[
\boxed{
\left(
\wp,\dim E,(d_1,\ldots,d_{\dim E})
\right)
=
\left(
\wp,6,(6,8,10,12,13,14)
\right),
}
\]

where \(\wp\) is the unique positive solution of

\[
\boxed{2^\wp=\sqrt2(3^\wp-1)}.
\]
